title: Drones, Missiles, and the U.S. Munitions Shortage
gist: After a five-month Iran war (Operation Epic Fury) drained US precision-missile stocks, CNAS models a Taiwan war and finds cheap long-range drones ('affordable mass') cannot replace high-end missiles because of range, hard-target and cost-per-effect limits, but mixed salvos of scout drones plus a few LRASMs/JASSM-ERs cut costs sharply (e.g., $9.4M vs $19.2M per Renhai cruiser kill; ~$184M vs $826M to blanket Huian Air Base); it urges multiyear procurement for both high-end missiles and thousands of producible low-cost munitions.

insights.claim: Just five months of on-and-off war with Iran caused the Department of War to burn through its stores of long-range precision-guided munitions, forcing a search for cheaper alternatives that can be produced faster.
